# kslides

> kslides is a Kotlin DSL for creating [reveal.js](https://revealjs.com) presentations. Slides are authored in Markdown, HTML, or the Kotlin HTML DSL. Output can be static HTML files (for Netlify/GitHub Pages) or served dynamically via an embedded Ktor HTTP server.

## Quick Start

New presentations should be created from the [kslides-template](https://github.com/kslides/kslides-template) repository. The template includes build configuration, deployment setup, and a starter presentation.

The `kslides-init.sh` script automates that setup — it clones the template, strips its git history, renames the project and presentation title, and initializes a fresh repository:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kslides/kslides/master/kslides-init.sh | bash -s -- my-talk --title "My Talk"
```

## Core Concepts

### DSL Structure

A presentation is defined using nested Kotlin DSL blocks:

```kotlin
kslides {
  output {}                 // Configure filesystem or HTTP output
  kslidesConfig {}          // Global kslides settings
  presentationConfig {}     // Default reveal.js config for all presentations
  css {}                    // Global CSS (Kotlin CSS DSL or raw strings)

  presentation {
    path = "myslides.html"
    presentationConfig {}   // Override config for this presentation
    css {}                  // Presentation-specific CSS

    markdownSlide { content { "# Hello" } }
    htmlSlide { content { "<h1>Hello</h1>" } }
    dslSlide { content { h1 { +"Hello" } } }
    verticalSlides {
      dslSlide { content { h2 { +"Vertical 1" } } }
      dslSlide { content { h2 { +"Vertical 2" } } }
    }
  }
}
```

### Three Slide Types

- **markdownSlide** — Content is a Markdown string
- **htmlSlide** — Content is a raw HTML string
- **dslSlide** — Content uses kotlinx.html DSL (supports `playground{}`, `diagram{}`, `mermaid()`, `codeSnippet{}`, `letsPlot{}`)

`letsPlot{}` lives in the optional `kslides-letsplot` module; the others are in `kslides-core`.

### Configuration Cascade

Configuration merges hierarchically: global `presentationConfig{}` → per-presentation `presentationConfig{}` → per-slide `slideConfig{}`. Each level overrides its parent.

Sub-configs within `presentationConfig{}`: `menuConfig{}`, `copyCodeConfig{}`, `playgroundConfig{}`, `letsPlotIframeConfig{}`, `slideConfig{}`, `diagramConfig{}`, `customTheme{}`.

`copyCodeConfig{}` configures the reveal.js CopyCode button (requires `enableCodeCopy = true`): `button` (`ALWAYS`/`HOVER`/`FALSE`) and `display` (`TEXT`/`ICONS`/`BOTH`) typed enums, `copy`/`copied` labels, `timeout`, button colors/borders, and `scale`/`offset`/`radius` sizing.

### Output Modes

Configured in the `output{}` block:
- **Filesystem** (`enableFileSystem = true`): Writes static HTML to the `docs/` directory. Playground, Lets-Plot, and kroki content generates separate files in `docs/playground/`, `docs/letsPlot/`, `docs/kroki/`.
- **HTTP** (`enableHttp = true`): Starts a Ktor CIO server (default port 8080). Static resources served from `src/main/resources/public/`.

`devMode = true` (HTTP only) adds live reload for local authoring: each served page embeds a client that connects to a `/kslides-reload` websocket and reloads when the server restarts, restoring the current slide and fragment from `sessionStorage`. Because slide content is compiled Kotlin, picking up an edit requires restarting the JVM — the `kslides-dev.sh` script watches sources and does the rebuild/restart automatically. (`./gradlew -t run` does not work for this: Gradle continuous build cannot restart a blocking server task.)

`followAlong = true` (HTTP only) adds follow-along presenting: the presenter opens a deck with `?present=<token>` — the presenter URLs are logged at startup — and every other visitor's browser follows the presenter's slide and fragment position live over a `/kslides-follow` websocket. Viewers get a badge they can click to break away and navigate freely, then click again to rejoin; late joiners land on the presenter's current slide. Viewers are read-only by construction (the server ignores their frames). One presenter per deck: a newcomer with a valid token supersedes the previous connection, which demotes itself to a viewer. Set `presenterToken` for a fixed token instead of a random one per launch. This is lightweight, demo-grade auth — the token travels in the URL.

`pdf { }` inside `output { }` configures PDF export (consumed by the `kslides-export` module, see below): `outputDir` (default `build/pdf`), `pageWidth`/`pageHeight` as CSS lengths (default: the deck's own print CSS decides), `exclude(...)` for per-presentation opt-out, `previewPng` to also capture a first-slide screenshot, `browserChannel` (`"chrome"`/`"msedge"`) to drive an installed browser instead of downloading Chromium, and `readyTimeoutMillis`/`settleMillis` timing knobs.

### DslSlide-Specific Features

- `playground {}` — Embeds an interactive [Kotlin Playground](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin-playground) iframe
- `mermaid(source)` — Renders a [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org) diagram client-side from a runtime bundled with kslides. No network access or external server, so decks work offline. Mermaid's dark theme is selected automatically for dark reveal.js themes; diagrams render lazily as their slide becomes visible. Since it takes a `String`, the source can come from `include()`.
- `diagram {}` — Generates diagrams via [Kroki](https://kroki.io/) (PlantUML, Mermaid, Graphviz, etc.), rendered server-side to a static image. The Kroki endpoint is configurable via `diagramConfig.krokiUrl`; a local Kroki server can be started from the `kroki/` directory with `docker-compose up -d` to avoid public-server rate limits. Prefer `mermaid()` for Mermaid diagrams; use `diagram {}` for formats Mermaid doesn't cover.
- `codeSnippet {}` — Syntax-highlighted code block with reveal.js highlight plugin
- `letsPlot {}` — Embeds [Lets-Plot](https://lets-plot.org/kotlin/) visualization iframes (requires the `kslides-letsplot` module). The JS runtime version is configurable via `kslidesConfig.letsPlotJsVersion`.

### Utility Functions

- `include(src)` — Include code from a file path or URL (preferred over inline code)
- `slideDefinition(source, token)` — Generate a slide showing the source of another slide, delimited by `token`. Takes a trailing `SlideConfig.() -> Unit` block for per-slide configuration, e.g. `slideDefinition(src, token) { codeFontSize = "0.40em" }`
- `githubRawUrl()` — Generate raw GitHub content URLs for `include()` calls
- `fragment()` — Wrap content in reveal.js fragments for animation
- `permuteBy()` — Generate animation step permutations
- `unorderedList()`, `orderedList()` — List helpers for DslSlides
- `headRow()`, `bodyRow()` — Table helpers for DslSlides

### CSS

CSS can be specified three ways:
1. Kotlin CSS DSL in `css {}` blocks
2. Raw CSS strings via `css += "..."`
3. External file at `src/main/resources/slides.css` (embedded into output)

CSS blocks can appear at global, presentation, or inline level. Unlike HTML, CSS blocks can be placed near the slides that reference them.

## Configuration Options

### PresentationConfig

All [reveal.js configuration options](https://revealjs.com/config/) are exposed as type-safe properties: `transition`, `transitionSpeed`, `controls`, `progress`, `center`, `loop`, `hash`, `autoSlide`, `slideNumber`, `mouseWheel`, `width`, `height`, `margin`, `theme`, `highlight`, etc.

kslides-specific options include: `title`, `theme` (enum: BLACK, WHITE, LEAGUE, BEIGE, SKY, NIGHT, SERIF, SIMPLE, SOLARIZED, BLOOD, MOON, DRACULA), `highlight` (MONOKAI, ZENBURN), `enableSpeakerNotes`, `enableMenu`, `enableCodeCopy`, `topLeftHref`/`topRightHref` (corner links), `gaPropertyId`.

### ThemeConfig (`customTheme{}`)

`customTheme{}` inside `presentationConfig{}` layers typed overrides on a stock reveal.js theme, so brand styling does not require hand-written CSS. It cascades global → presentation like every other config, and only assigned properties are emitted — as a `<style id="custom-theme">` block layered after the base theme's stylesheet, so `slides.css` and `css{}` rules can still override it.

```kotlin
presentationConfig {
  customTheme {
    baseTheme = PresentationTheme.WHITE       // stock theme to layer on; wins over `theme`
    backgroundColor = Color("#f8f5ef")
    mainColor = Color("#1a1a2e")
    headingColor = Color("#0f4c81")
    headingTextTransform = TextTransform.none // disable the stock themes' UPPERCASE headings
    codeFont = "Menlo, Consolas, monospace"
    customProperty("--r-heading-letter-spacing", "0.02em")
    logo("images/logo.png", position = LogoPosition.BOTTOM_RIGHT, size = 90.px)
  }
}
```

Eighteen typed properties map 1:1 to reveal.js `--r-*` theme variables: `backgroundColor`, `mainColor`, `mainFont`, `mainFontSize`, `headingColor`, `headingFont`, `headingTextTransform`, `headingFontWeight`, `heading1Size`–`heading4Size`, `codeFont`, `linkColor`, `linkColorHover`, `selectionColor`, `selectionBackgroundColor`, `blockMargin`. Values use kotlinx.css types (`Color`, `LinearDimension`, `TextTransform`). `customProperty(name, value)` passes through variables the DSL does not model (the name must start with `--`). `logo(src, position, size, margin, opacity, href)` pins a brand image to a corner of every slide and every exported PDF page; `position` is a `LogoPosition` (TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT), and without an `href` the logo ignores pointer events.

### SlideConfig

Per-slide options: `backgroundColor`, `backgroundImage`, `backgroundSize`, `backgroundPosition`, `backgroundRepeat`, `backgroundOpacity`, `backgroundVideo`, `backgroundVideoLoop`, `backgroundVideoMuted`, `backgroundIframe`.

Font sizing: `fontSize` (inline `font-size` on the slide's `<section>`, any CSS length), `codeFontSize` (font size for `<pre>` code blocks, emitted as a generated CSS class plus a head rule), and `codeWrap` (wrap long code lines instead of overflowing). These resolve through the global → presentation → slide cascade, so a deck-wide default can be set once in `presentationConfig { slideConfig { } }`. They are resolved *per-slide*, so setting them in a `verticalSlides { slideConfig { } }` block is silently ignored — a stack-level `slideConfig{}` only carries reveal.js `data-*` options.

### Slide Properties

Common slide properties: `id`, `classes`, `style`, `hidden`, `uncounted`, `autoAnimate`, `autoAnimateRestart`. MarkdownSlides also support `filename` for external markdown files.

## PDF Export

The optional `kslides-export` module turns a deck into a PDF with one command. `exportPdf()` accepts the same block as `kslides{}`, builds the presentations, serves them from an ephemeral-port Ktor server, and prints each deck through headless Chromium (Playwright), waiting for reveal.js' `pdf-ready` event and any Mermaid diagrams before printing:

```kotlin
fun KSlides.myDeck() {
  presentation { markdownSlide { content { "# My Deck" } } }
}

fun main() {
  exportPdf { myDeck() }          // every presentation -> one PDF each
  // exportPdf("demo") { myDeck() } // just the presentation at /demo.html
}
```

Settings come from the `pdf { }` block in `output { }` (above). On first use Playwright downloads its own browsers; set `browserChannel` to skip that and drive an installed Chrome/Edge. Content fetched at render time still needs its backing service — Kroki `diagram{}` slides need a reachable Kroki server, while native `mermaid()` renders offline. Keep the dependency out of a runnable fat JAR by putting the export entry point in its own source set.

## Tooling Entry Points

- `buildKSlides(block)` — evaluates and validates the DSL without emitting any output, returning the populated `KSlides`
- `KSlides.startHttpServer(port, wait)` — starts the HTTP-mode Ktor server programmatically (port `0` picks an ephemeral port) and returns a closeable `KSlidesHttpServer` exposing the bound `port`
- `kslidesTest(block)` — evaluates the DSL with both output modes forced off, for tests

## Project Structure

- `kslides-core/` — Core DSL library
- `kslides-examples/` — Example presentations with main entry point
- `kslides-export/` — One-command PDF export via headless Chromium (Playwright)
- `kslides-letsplot/` — Lets-Plot chart integration module
- `kslides-init.sh` — Scaffolds a new presentation project from `kslides-template`
- `kslides-dev.sh` — Live-reload supervisor: watches sources, rebuilds, restarts the app

## Dependencies

Published to [Maven Central](https://central.sonatype.com/namespace/com.kslides) under the `com.kslides` group. Add to your project:

```kotlin
repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}
dependencies {
    implementation("com.kslides:kslides-core:1.3.0")
    // Optional: implementation("com.kslides:kslides-letsplot:1.3.0")
    // Optional: implementation("com.kslides:kslides-export:1.3.0")
}
```
